div.div:
Estimates (assumptions)
• 1B pages per month → ~400 pages/s, peak ~800
• Average HTML 500 KB (as in the chapter) → 500 TB/month raw, ~100 TB gzipped
• Network: 400 × 500 KB = 200 MB/s ≈ 1.6 Gbit/s
• Little's law: 400 pages/s × 2 s = ~800 concurrent fetches
• Bloom filter for 1B URLs at 1% false positives ≈ 1.2 GB
• Metadata: 1B × ~200 B ≈ 200 GB
Queue partition key
hash(host) via consistent hashing: all URLs of a host live in one Frontier shard → politeness is enforced locally, no distributed locks. Cost: a hot host sits entirely in one shard; a new shard moves ~1/N of hosts.
Duplicates and traps
• Normalize URLs before any check
• URL Seen? — Bloom: a false "seen" skips a few new URLs but never downloads twice
• Content Seen? — sha256 of content: the same page under different URLs
• URL length ≤ 2048, depth ≤ 15, daily page limit per host
Politeness
robots.txt (24 h cache, crawl-delay); 1 request per host at a time + pause; the pause grows on 429/503 and rising latency; User-Agent with contact info.
Failure: a site takes 30 s to respond
Connect 3 s, total 10 s → abort, nack(timeout). Frontier doubles the host pause; after 3 timeouts in a row the host is paused for an hour. Fetches are async: a slow host holds 1 slot out of ~200, the rest keep downloading.
Failure: a worker dies mid-download
The URL is leased for 60 s. No ack → Lease Reaper returns it to the host queue, attempts+1, after 3 — dead. S3 PUT is atomic: a partial file never appears. The Kafka event is published only after the S3 write. A retry is safe: the S3 key is deterministic, Content Seen? drops the duplicate.
What breaks first at ×10 (4,000 pages/s)
1. Network (~16 Gbit/s) and storage (~5 PB/month raw) → gzip, store only changed pages.
2. Frontier Store memory: hundreds of millions of URLs in Redis → cold URLs to disk, Redis only as a buffer.
3. Politeness: a single host cannot go 10× faster — you need wider host coverage.
